[878](#878)
[879](#879)impl<T: Config> OnQueueChanged<ParaId> for Pallet<T> {
[880](#880)	fn on_queue_changed(para: ParaId, fp: QueueFootprint) {
[882](#882)		let QueueConfigData { resume_threshold, suspend_threshold, .. } = <QueueConfig<T>>::get();
[883](#883)
[884](#884)		let mut suspended_channels = <InboundXcmpSuspended<T>>::get();
[885](#885)		let suspended = suspended_channels.contains(¶);
[886](#886)
[887](#887)		if suspended && fp.ready_pages <= resume_threshold {
[888](#888)			if let Err(err) = Self::send_signal(para, ChannelSignal::Resume) {
[889](#889)				tracing::error!(
[890](#890)					target: LOG_TARGET,
[891](#891)					error=?err,
[892](#892)					sibling=?para,
[893](#893)					"defensive: Could not send resumption signal to inbound channel of sibling; channel remains suspended."
[894](#894)				);
[895](#895)			} else {
[896](#896)				suspended_channels.remove(¶);
[897](#897)				<InboundXcmpSuspended<T>>::put(suspended_channels);
[898](#898)			}
[899](#899)		} else if !suspended && fp.ready_pages >= suspend_threshold {
[900](#900)			tracing::warn!(target: LOG_TARGET, sibling=?para, "XCMP queue for sibling is full; suspending channel.");
[901](#901)
[902](#902)			if let Err(err) = Self::send_signal(para, ChannelSignal::Suspend) {
[903](#903)				tracing::error!(
[905](#905)					target: LOG_TARGET, error=?err,
[906](#906)					"defensive: Could not send suspension signal; future messages may be dropped."
[907](#907)				);
[908](#908)			} else if let Err(err) = suspended_channels.try_insert(para) {
[909](#909)				tracing::error!(
[910](#910)					target: LOG_TARGET,
[911](#911)					error=?err,
[912](#912)					sibling=?para,
[913](#913)					"Too many channels suspended; cannot suspend sibling; further messages may be dropped."
[914](#914)				);
[915](#915)			} else {
[916](#916)				<InboundXcmpSuspended<T>>::put(suspended_channels);
[917](#917)			}
[918](#918)		}
[919](#919)	}
[920](#920)}
[921](#921)
[922](#922)impl<T: Config> QueuePausedQuery<ParaId> for Pallet<T> {
[923](#923)	fn is_paused(para: &ParaId) -> bool {
[924](#924)		if !QueueSuspended::<T>::get() {
[925](#925)			return false;
[926](#926)		}
[927](#927)
[928](#928)		let sender_origin = T::ControllerOriginConverter::convert_origin(
[930](#930)			(Parent, Parachain((*para).into())),
[931](#931)			OriginKind::Superuser,
[932](#932)		);
[933](#933)		let is_controller =
[934](#934)			sender_origin.map_or(false, |origin| T::ControllerOrigin::try_origin(origin).is_ok());
[935](#935)
[936](#936)		!is_controller
[937](#937)	}
[938](#938)}
[939](#939)
[940](#940)#[derive(Copy, Clone)]
[942](#942)enum XcmEncoding {
[943](#943)	Simple,
[948](#948)	Double,
[956](#956)}
[957](#957)
[958](#958)impl<T: Config> XcmpMessageHandler for Pallet<T> {
[959](#959)	fn handle_xcmp_messages<'a, I: Iterator<Item = (ParaId, RelayBlockNumber, &'a [u8])>>(
[960](#960)		iter: I,
[961](#961)		max_weight: Weight,
[962](#962)	) -> Weight {
[963](#963)		let mut meter = WeightMeter::with_limit(max_weight);
[964](#964)
[965](#965)		let mut known_xcm_senders = BTreeSet::new();
[966](#966)		for (sender, _sent_at, mut data) in iter {
[967](#967)			let format = match XcmpMessageFormat::decode(&mut data) {
[968](#968)				Ok(f) => f,
[969](#969)				Err(_) => {
[970](#970)					defensive!("Unknown XCMP message format - dropping");
[971](#971)					continue;
[972](#972)				},
[973](#973)			};
[974](#974)
[975](#975)			match format {
[976](#976)				XcmpMessageFormat::Signals => {
[977](#977)					let mut signal_count = 0;
[978](#978)					while !data.is_empty() && signal_count < MAX_SIGNALS_PER_PAGE {
[979](#979)						signal_count += 1;
[980](#980)						match ChannelSignal::decode(&mut data) {
[981](#981)							Ok(ChannelSignal::Suspend) => {
[982](#982)								if meter.try_consume(T::WeightInfo::suspend_channel()).is_err() {
[983](#983)									defensive!(
[984](#984)										"Not enough weight to process suspend signal - dropping"
[985](#985)									);
[986](#986)									break;
[987](#987)								}
[988](#988)								Self::suspend_channel(sender)
[989](#989)							},
[990](#990)							Ok(ChannelSignal::Resume) => {
[991](#991)								if meter.try_consume(T::WeightInfo::resume_channel()).is_err() {
[992](#992)									defensive!(
[993](#993)										"Not enough weight to process resume signal - dropping"
[994](#994)									);
[995](#995)									break;
[996](#996)								}
[997](#997)								Self::resume_channel(sender)
[998](#998)							},
[999](#999)							Err(_) => {
[1000](#1000)								defensive!("Undecodable channel signal - dropping");
[1001](#1001)								break;
[1002](#1002)							},
[1003](#1003)						}
[1004](#1004)					}
[1005](#1005)				},
[1006](#1006)				XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedVersionedXcm |
[1007](#1007)				XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedOpaqueVersionedXcm => {
[1008](#1008)					let encoding = match format {
[1009](#1009)						XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedVersionedXcm => XcmEncoding::Simple,
[1010](#1010)						XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedOpaqueVersionedXcm => {
[1011](#1011)							let mut all_channels = <OutboundXcmpStatus<T>>::get();
[1012](#1012)							if let Some(channel_details) =
[1013](#1013)								Self::try_get_or_insert_outbound_channel(&mut all_channels, sender)
[1014](#1014)							{
[1015](#1015)								channel_details
[1016](#1016)									.flags
[1017](#1017)									.notice_concatenated_opaque_versioned_xcm_support();
[1018](#1018)							}
[1019](#1019)							<OutboundXcmpStatus<T>>::put(all_channels);
[1020](#1020)
[1021](#1021)							XcmEncoding::Double
[1022](#1022)						},
[1023](#1023)						_ => {
[1024](#1024)							continue;
[1026](#1026)						},
[1027](#1027)					};
[1028](#1028)
[1029](#1029)					let mut is_first_sender_batch = known_xcm_senders.insert(sender);
[1030](#1030)					if is_first_sender_batch {
[1031](#1031)						if meter
[1032](#1032)							.try_consume(T::WeightInfo::uncached_enqueue_xcmp_messages())
[1033](#1033)							.is_err()
[1034](#1034)						{
[1035](#1035)							defensive!(
[1036](#1036)								"Out of weight: cannot enqueue XCMP messages; dropping page; \
[1037](#1037)                                    Used weight: ",
[1038](#1038)								meter.consumed_ratio()
[1039](#1039)							);
[1040](#1040)							continue;
[1041](#1041)						}
[1042](#1042)					}
[1043](#1043)
[1044](#1044)					let mut can_process_next_batch = true;
[1045](#1045)					while can_process_next_batch {
[1046](#1046)						let batch = match Self::take_first_concatenated_xcms(
[1047](#1047)							&mut data,
[1048](#1048)							encoding,
[1049](#1049)							XCM_BATCH_SIZE,
[1050](#1050)							&mut meter,
[1051](#1051)						) {
[1052](#1052)							Ok(batch) => batch,
[1053](#1053)							Err(batch) => {
[1054](#1054)								can_process_next_batch = false;
[1055](#1055)								defensive!(
[1056](#1056)									"HRMP inbound decode stream broke; page will be dropped."
[1057](#1057)								);
[1058](#1058)								batch
[1059](#1059)							},
[1060](#1060)						};
[1061](#1061)						if batch.is_empty() {
[1062](#1062)							break;
[1063](#1063)						}
[1064](#1064)
[1065](#1065)						if let Err(()) = Self::enqueue_xcmp_messages(
[1066](#1066)							sender,
[1067](#1067)							&batch,
[1068](#1068)							is_first_sender_batch,
[1069](#1069)							&mut meter,
[1070](#1070)						) {
[1071](#1071)							break;
[1072](#1072)						}
[1073](#1073)						is_first_sender_batch = false;
[1074](#1074)					}
[1075](#1075)				},
[1076](#1076)				XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedEncodedBlob => {
[1077](#1077)					defensive!("Blob messages are unhandled - dropping");
[1078](#1078)					continue;
[1079](#1079)				},
[1080](#1080)			}
[1081](#1081)		}
[1082](#1082)
[1083](#1083)		meter.consumed()
[1084](#1084)	}
[1085](#1085)}
[1086](#1086)
[1087](#1087)impl<T: Config> XcmpMessageSource for Pallet<T> {
[1088](#1088)	fn take_outbound_messages(
[1089](#1089)		maximum_channels: usize,
[1090](#1090)		excluded_recipients: &[ParaId],
[1091](#1091)	) -> Vec<(ParaId, Vec<u8>)> {
[1092](#1092)		let mut statuses = <OutboundXcmpStatus<T>>::get().into_inner();
[1093](#1093)		let old_statuses_len = statuses.len();
[1094](#1094)		let max_message_count = statuses.len().min(maximum_channels);
[1095](#1095)		let mut result = Vec::with_capacity(max_message_count);
[1096](#1096)
[1097](#1097)		statuses.retain_mut(|status| {
[1098](#1098)			let OutboundChannelDetails {
[1099](#1099)				recipient: para_id,
[1100](#1100)				state: outbound_state,
[1101](#1101)				signals_exist,
[1102](#1102)				first_index,
[1103](#1103)				last_index,
[1104](#1104)				flags,
[1105](#1105)				queued_bytes,
[1106](#1106)			} = status;
[1107](#1107)
[1108](#1108)			let (max_size_now, max_size_ever) = match T::ChannelInfo::get_channel_status(*para_id) {
[1109](#1109)				ChannelStatus::Closed => {
[1110](#1110)					for i in *first_index..*last_index {
[1113](#1113)						<OutboundXcmpMessages<T>>::remove(*para_id, i);
[1114](#1114)					}
[1115](#1115)					if *signals_exist {
[1116](#1116)						<SignalMessages<T>>::remove(*para_id);
[1117](#1117)					}
[1118](#1118)					return false;
[1119](#1119)				},
[1120](#1120)				ChannelStatus::Full => return true,
[1121](#1121)				ChannelStatus::Ready(max_size_now, max_size_ever) => (max_size_now, max_size_ever),
[1122](#1122)			};
[1123](#1123)
[1124](#1124)			if excluded_recipients.contains(para_id) {
[1126](#1126)				return true;
[1127](#1127)			}
[1128](#1128)
[1129](#1129)			if result.len() == max_message_count {
[1131](#1131)				return true;
[1134](#1134)			}
[1135](#1135)
[1136](#1136)			let page = 'page_fetch: {
[1137](#1137)				if *signals_exist {
[1138](#1138)					let page = <SignalMessages<T>>::get(*para_id);
[1139](#1139)					defensive_assert!(!page.is_empty(), "Signals must exist");
[1140](#1140)
[1141](#1141)					if page.len() < max_size_now {
[1142](#1142)						<SignalMessages<T>>::remove(*para_id);
[1143](#1143)						*signals_exist = false;
[1144](#1144)						break 'page_fetch page;
[1145](#1145)					}
[1146](#1146)
[1147](#1147)					defensive!("Signals should fit into a single page");
[1148](#1148)					return true;
[1149](#1149)				}
[1150](#1150)
[1151](#1151)				if *outbound_state == OutboundState::Suspended {
[1152](#1152)					return true;
[1154](#1154)				}
[1155](#1155)
[1156](#1156)				if last_index > first_index {
[1157](#1157)					let page = <OutboundXcmpMessages<T>>::get(*para_id, *first_index);
[1158](#1158)					if page.len() < max_size_now {
[1159](#1159)						<OutboundXcmpMessages<T>>::remove(*para_id, *first_index);
[1160](#1160)						*first_index += 1;
[1161](#1161)						*queued_bytes = queued_bytes.saturating_sub(page.len() as u32);
[1162](#1162)						break 'page_fetch page;
[1163](#1163)					}
[1164](#1164)				}
[1165](#1165)
[1166](#1166)				if flags.should_send_concatenated_opaque_versioned_xcm_notification() {
[1170](#1170)					match WeakBoundedVec::try_from(XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedOpaqueVersionedXcm.encode()) {
[1171](#1171)						Ok(page) => {
[1172](#1172)							flags.notice_concatenated_opaque_versioned_xcm_notification_sent();
[1173](#1173)							break 'page_fetch page;
[1174](#1174)						},
[1175](#1175)						Err(_) => {
[1176](#1176)							defensive!("XcmpMessageFormat should fit into a single page");
[1177](#1177)							return true;
[1178](#1178)						}
[1179](#1179)					};
[1180](#1180)				}
[1181](#1181)
[1182](#1182)				return true;
[1183](#1183)			};
[1184](#1184)
[1185](#1185)			if first_index == last_index {
[1186](#1186)				*first_index = 0;
[1187](#1187)				*last_index = 0;
[1188](#1188)				*queued_bytes = 0;
[1189](#1189)			}
[1190](#1190)
[1191](#1191)			if page.len() > max_size_ever {
[1192](#1192)				defensive!("WARNING: oversize message in queue - dropping");
[1196](#1196)			} else {
[1197](#1197)				result.push((*para_id, page.into_inner()));
[1198](#1198)			}
[1199](#1199)
[1200](#1200)			let max_total_size = match T::ChannelInfo::get_channel_info(*para_id) {
[1201](#1201)				Some(channel_info) => channel_info.max_total_size,
[1202](#1202)				None => {
[1203](#1203)					tracing::warn!(target: LOG_TARGET, "calling `get_channel_info` with no RelevantMessagingState?!");
[1204](#1204)					MAX_POSSIBLE_ALLOCATION
[1206](#1206)				},
[1207](#1207)			};
[1208](#1208)			let threshold = max_total_size.saturating_div(delivery_fee_constants::THRESHOLD_FACTOR);
[1209](#1209)			if *queued_bytes <= threshold {
[1210](#1210)				Self::decrease_fee_factor(*para_id);
[1211](#1211)			}
[1212](#1212)
[1213](#1213)			true
[1214](#1214)		});
[1215](#1215)		debug_assert!(!statuses.iter().any(|s| s.signals_exist), "Signals should be handled");
[1216](#1216)		let mut statuses = BoundedVec::defensive_truncate_from(statuses);
[1217](#1217)
[1218](#1218)		result.sort_by_key(|(recipient, _msg)| *recipient);
[1221](#1221)
[1222](#1222)		let pruned = old_statuses_len - statuses.len();
[1224](#1224)		let _ = statuses.try_rotate_left(result.len().saturating_sub(pruned)).defensive_proof(
[1229](#1229)			"Could not store HRMP channels config. Some HRMP channels may be broken.",
[1230](#1230)		);
[1231](#1231)
[1232](#1232)		<OutboundXcmpStatus<T>>::put(statuses);
[1233](#1233)
[1234](#1234)		result
[1235](#1235)	}
[1236](#1236)}

[1238](#1238)impl<T: Config> SendXcm for Pallet<T> {
[1240](#1240)	type Ticket = (ParaId, VersionedXcm<()>);
[1241](#1241)
[1242](#1242)	fn validate(
[1243](#1243)		dest: &mut Option<Location>,
[1244](#1244)		msg: &mut Option<Xcm<()>>,
[1245](#1245)	) -> SendResult<(ParaId, VersionedXcm<()>)> {
[1246](#1246)		let d = dest.take().ok_or(SendError::MissingArgument)?;
[1247](#1247)
[1248](#1248)		match d.unpack() {
[1249](#1249)			(1, [Parachain(id)]) => {
[1251](#1251)				let xcm = msg.take().ok_or(SendError::MissingArgument)?;
[1252](#1252)				let id = ParaId::from(*id);
[1253](#1253)				let price = T::PriceForSiblingDelivery::price_for_delivery(id, &xcm);
[1254](#1254)				let versioned_xcm = T::VersionWrapper::wrap_version(&d, xcm)
[1255](#1255)					.map_err(|()| SendError::DestinationUnsupported)?;
[1256](#1256)				versioned_xcm
[1257](#1257)					.check_is_decodable()
[1258](#1258)					.map_err(|()| SendError::ExceedsMaxMessageSize)?;
[1259](#1259)
[1260](#1260)				Ok(((id, versioned_xcm), price))
[1261](#1261)			},
[1262](#1262)			_ => {
[1263](#1263)				*dest = Some(d);
[1266](#1266)				Err(SendError::NotApplicable)
[1267](#1267)			},
[1268](#1268)		}
[1269](#1269)	}
[1270](#1270)
[1271](#1271)	fn deliver((recipient, xcm): (ParaId, VersionedXcm<()>)) -> Result<XcmHash, SendError> {
[1272](#1272)		let hash = xcm.using_encoded(sp_io::hashing::blake2_256);
[1273](#1273)
[1274](#1274)		let mut encoding = XcmEncoding::Simple;
[1275](#1275)		let mut all_channels = <OutboundXcmpStatus<T>>::get();
[1276](#1276)		if let Some(channel_details) = Self::try_get_outbound_channel(&mut all_channels, recipient)
[1277](#1277)		{
[1278](#1278)			if channel_details.flags.has_concatenated_opaque_versioned_xcm_support() {
[1279](#1279)				encoding = XcmEncoding::Double;
[1280](#1280)			}
[1281](#1281)		}
[1282](#1282)
[1283](#1283)		let result = match encoding {
[1284](#1284)			XcmEncoding::Simple => {
[1285](#1285)				Self::send_fragment(recipient, XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedVersionedXcm, xcm)
[1286](#1286)			},
[1287](#1287)			XcmEncoding::Double => Self::send_fragment(
[1288](#1288)				recipient,
[1289](#1289)				XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedOpaqueVersionedXcm,
[1290](#1290)				xcm.encode(),
[1291](#1291)			),
[1292](#1292)		};
[1293](#1293)		match result {
[1294](#1294)			Ok(_) => {
[1295](#1295)				Self::deposit_event(Event::XcmpMessageSent { message_hash: hash });
[1296](#1296)				Ok(hash)
[1297](#1297)			},
[1298](#1298)			Err(e) => {
[1299](#1299)				tracing::error!(target: LOG_TARGET, error=?e, "Deliver error");
[1300](#1300)				Err(SendError::Transport(e.into()))
[1301](#1301)			},
[1302](#1302)		}
[1303](#1303)	}
[1304](#1304)}

[1306](#1306)impl<T: Config> InspectMessageQueues for Pallet<T> {
[1307](#1307)	fn clear_messages() {
[1308](#1308)		let _ = OutboundXcmpMessages::<T>::clear(u32::MAX, None);
[1310](#1310)		OutboundXcmpStatus::<T>::mutate(|details_vec| {
[1311](#1311)			for details in details_vec {
[1312](#1312)				details.first_index = 0;
[1313](#1313)				details.last_index = 0;
[1314](#1314)				details.queued_bytes = 0;
[1315](#1315)			}
[1316](#1316)		});
[1317](#1317)	}
[1318](#1318)
[1319](#1319)	fn get_messages() -> Vec<(VersionedLocation, Vec<VersionedXcm<()>>)> {
[1320](#1320)		use xcm::prelude::*;
[1321](#1321)
[1322](#1322)		OutboundXcmpMessages::<T>::iter()
[1323](#1323)			.map(|(para_id, _, messages)| {
[1324](#1324)				let data = &mut &messages[..];
[1325](#1325)
[1326](#1326)				let decoded_format = XcmpMessageFormat::decode(data).unwrap();
[1327](#1327)				let mut decoded_messages = Vec::new();
[1328](#1328)				while !data.is_empty() {
[1329](#1329)					let message_bytes = match decoded_format {
[1330](#1330)						XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedVersionedXcm => {
[1331](#1331)							Self::take_first_concatenated_xcm(data, &mut WeightMeter::new())
[1332](#1332)						},
[1333](#1333)						XcmpMessageFormat::ConcatenatedOpaqueVersionedXcm => {
[1334](#1334)							Self::take_first_concatenated_opaque_xcm(data)
[1335](#1335)						},
[1336](#1336)						unexpected_format => {
[1337](#1337)							panic!("Unexpected XCMP format: {unexpected_format:?}!")
[1338](#1338)						},
[1339](#1339)					}
[1340](#1340)					.unwrap();
[1341](#1341)					let decoded_message = VersionedXcm::<()>::decode_with_depth_limit(
[1342](#1342)						MAX_XCM_DECODE_DEPTH,
[1343](#1343)						&mut &message_bytes[..],
[1344](#1344)					)
[1345](#1345)					.unwrap();
[1346](#1346)					decoded_messages.push(decoded_message);
[1347](#1347)				}
[1348](#1348)
[1349](#1349)				(
[1350](#1350)					VersionedLocation::from(Location::new(1, Parachain(para_id.into()))),
[1351](#1351)					decoded_messages,
[1352](#1352)				)
[1353](#1353)			})
[1354](#1354)			.collect()
[1355](#1355)	}

# cumulus_pallet_xcmp_queue::pallet - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/cumulus-pallet-xcmp-queue/0.30.0/cumulus_pallet_xcmp_queue/pallet/index.html

## Expand description

The `pallet` module in each FRAME pallet hosts the most important items needed
to construct this pallet.

The main components of this pallet are:

- `Pallet`- The subset of the functions that are dispatchable can be identified either in the
`dispatchables``Call`

- The subset of the functions that are dispatchable can be identified either in the
- `storage_types`- *Type Definitions*
- `Config`
- `Event`- `Error`- *Enums*

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [dispatchables](https://docs.rs/dispatchables/index.html)
- Auto-generated docs-only module listing all defined dispatchables for this pallet.
- [storage_](https://docs.rs/storage_types/index.html)- types
- Auto-generated docs-only module listing all (public and private) defined storage types for this pallet.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Pallet](https://docs.rs/struct.Pallet.html)
- The `Pallet`struct, the main type that implements traits and standalone functions within the pallet.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [Call](https://docs.rs/enum.Call.html)
- Contains a variant per dispatchable extrinsic that this pallet has.
- [Error](https://docs.rs/enum.Error.html)
- The `Error`enum of this pallet.
- [Event](https://docs.rs/enum.Event.html)
- The `Event`enum of this pallet

## Traits[§](https://docs.rs#traits)

- [Config](https://docs.rs/trait.Config.html)
- Configuration trait of this pallet.

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [Inbound](https://docs.rs/type.InboundXcmpSuspended.html)- Xcmp - Suspended
- The suspended inbound XCMP channels. All others are not suspended.
- [Module](https://docs.rs/type.Module.html)- Deprecated
- Type alias to `Pallet`, to be used by`construct_runtime`.

# pallet_balances - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/pallet-balances/^50.0.0/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#balances-pallet)Balances Pallet

The Balances pallet provides functionality for handling accounts and balances for a single token.

It makes heavy use of concepts such as Holds and Freezes from the
[ frame_support::traits::fungible](https://docs.rs/frame-support/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/frame_support/traits/tokens/fungible/index.html) traits, therefore you should read and understand those docs
as a prerequisite to understanding this pallet.

Also see the [ frame_tokens](https://docs.rs/polkadot_sdk_docs/reference_docs/frame_tokens/index.html) reference docs for higher level information regarding the
place of this palet in FRAME.

[§](https://docs.rs#overview)Overview

The Balances pallet provides functions for:

- Getting and setting free balances.
- Retrieving total, reserved and unreserved balances.
- Repatriating a reserved balance to a beneficiary account that exists.
- Transferring a balance between accounts (when not reserved).
- Slashing an account balance.
- Account creation and removal.
- Managing total issuance.
- Setting and managing locks.

[§](https://docs.rs#terminology)Terminology

- **Reaping an account:**The act of removing an account by resetting its nonce. Happens after its total balance has become less than the Existential Deposit.

[§](https://docs.rs#implementations-1)Implementations

The Balances pallet provides implementations for the following [ fungible](https://docs.rs/frame-support/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/frame_support/traits/tokens/fungible/index.html) traits. If these
traits provide the functionality that you need, then you should avoid tight coupling with the
Balances pallet.

- `fungible::Inspect`
- `fungible::Mutate`
- `fungible::Unbalanced`
- `fungible::Balanced`
- `fungible::BalancedHold`
- `fungible::InspectHold`
- `fungible::MutateHold`
- `fungible::InspectFreeze`
- `fungible::MutateFreeze`
- `fungible::Imbalance`

It also implements the following [ Currency](https://docs.rs/frame-support/48.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/frame_support/traits/tokens/currency/trait.Currency.html) related traits, however they are deprecated and
will eventually be removed.

- `Currency`
- `ReservableCurrency`
- `NamedReservableCurrency`
- `LockableCurrency`
- `Imbalance`

[§](https://docs.rs#usage)Usage

The following examples show how to use the Balances pallet in your custom pallet.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-from-the-frame)Examples from the FRAME

The Contract pallet uses the `Currency` trait to handle gas payment, and its types inherit from
`Currency`:

```
use frame_support::traits::Currency;
pub type BalanceOf<T> = <<T as Config>::Currency as Currency<<T as frame_system::Config>::AccountId>>::Balance;
pub type NegativeImbalanceOf<T> = <<T as Config>::Currency as Currency<<T as frame_system::Config>::AccountId>>::NegativeImbalance;
```
The Staking pallet uses the `LockableCurrency` trait to lock a stash account’s funds:

```
use frame_support::traits::{WithdrawReasons, LockableCurrency};
use sp_runtime::traits::Bounded;
pub trait Config: frame_system::Config {
    type Currency: LockableCurrency<Self::AccountId, Moment=frame_system::pallet_prelude::BlockNumberFor<Self>>;
}
fn update_ledger<T: Config>(
    controller: &T::AccountId,
    ledger: &StakingLedger<T>
) {
    T::Currency::set_lock(
        STAKING_ID,
        &ledger.stash,
        ledger.total,
        WithdrawReasons::all()
    );
    // <Ledger<T>>::insert(controller, ledger); // Commented out as we don't have access to Staking's storage here.
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#genesis-config)Genesis config

The Balances pallet depends on the [ GenesisConfig](https://docs.rs/pallet/struct.GenesisConfig.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#assumptions)Assumptions

- Total issued balanced of all accounts should be less than `Config::Balance::max_value()`.
- Existential Deposit is set to a value greater than zero.

Note, you may find the Balances pallet still functions with an ED of zero when the
`insecure_zero_ed` cargo feature is enabled. However this is not a configuration which is
generally supported, nor will it be.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use weights::`- [WeightInfo](https://docs.rs/weights/trait.WeightInfo.html);
- `pub use`- [pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/index.html)::*;

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [migration](https://docs.rs/migration/index.html)
- [pallet](https://docs.rs/pallet/index.html)
- The `pallet`module in each FRAME pallet hosts the most important items needed to construct this pallet.
- [weights](https://docs.rs/weights/index.html)
- Autogenerated weights for `pallet_balances`

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Account](https://docs.rs/struct.AccountData.html)- Data
- All balance information for an account.
- [Balance](https://docs.rs/struct.BalanceLock.html)- Lock
- A single lock on a balance. There can be many of these on an account and they “overlap”, so the same balance is frozen by multiple locks.
- [Dust](https://docs.rs/struct.DustCleaner.html)- Cleaner
- [Extra](https://docs.rs/struct.ExtraFlags.html)- Flags
- [Negative](https://docs.rs/struct.NegativeImbalance.html)- Imbalance
- Opaque, move-only struct with private fields that serves as a token denoting that funds have been destroyed without any equal and opposite accounting.
- [Positive](https://docs.rs/struct.PositiveImbalance.html)- Imbalance
- Opaque, move-only struct with private fields that serves as a token denoting that funds have been created without any equal and opposite accounting.
- [Reserve](https://docs.rs/struct.ReserveData.html)- Data
- Store named reserved balance.

- Whether something should be interpreted as an increase or a decrease.

- Simplified reasons for withdrawing balance.

# polkadot_parachain_primitives - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/polkadot-parachain-primitives/^23.0.0/

## Expand description

Defines primitive types for creating or validating a parachain.

When compiled with standard library support, this crate exports a `wasm`
module that can be used to validate parachain WASM.

[§](https://docs.rs#parachain-wasm)Parachain WASM

Polkadot parachain WASM is in the form of a module which imports a memory
instance and exports a function `validate_block`.

`validate` accepts as input two `i32` values, representing a pointer/length pair
respectively, that encodes [ ValidationParams](https://docs.rs/primitives/struct.ValidationParams.html).

`validate` returns an `u64` which is a pointer to an `u8` array and its length.
The data in the array is expected to be a SCALE encoded
[ ValidationResult](https://docs.rs/primitives/struct.ValidationResult.html).

ASCII-diagram demonstrating the return data format:

The wasm-api (enabled only when `std` feature is not enabled and `wasm-api` feature is enabled)
provides utilities for setting up a parachain WASM module in Rust.

## Modules[§](https://docs.rs#modules)

- [primitives](https://docs.rs/primitives/index.html)
- Primitive types which are strictly necessary from a parachain-execution point of view.

---

# sp_tracing - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/sp-tracing/^19.0.0/

## Expand description

Substrate tracing primitives and macros.

To trace functions or individual code in Substrate, this crate provides [ within_span](https://docs.rs/macro.within_span.html)
and

[. See the individual docs for how to use these macros.](https://docs.rs/macro.enter_span.html)

`enter_span`Note that to allow traces from wasm execution environment there are
2 reserved identifiers for tracing `Field` recording, stored in the consts:
`WASM_TARGET_KEY` and `WASM_NAME_KEY` - if you choose to record fields, you
must ensure that your identifiers do not clash with either of these.

Additionally, we have a const: `WASM_TRACE_IDENTIFIER`, which holds a span name used
to signal that the ‘actual’ span name and target should be retrieved instead from
the associated Fields mentioned above.

Note: The `tracing` crate requires trace metadata to be static. This does not work
for wasm code in substrate, as it is regularly updated with new code from on-chain
events. The workaround for this is for the wasm tracing wrappers to put the
`name` and `target` data in the `values` map (normally they would be in the static
metadata assembled at compile time).

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [tracing_subscriber](https://docs.rs/tracing-subscriber/0.3.18/wasm32-unknown-unknown/tracing_subscriber/index.html);

- To prevent Out of Memory errors on the `DownwardMessageQueue`, an exponential fee factor (`DeliveryFeeFactor`) is set. The fee factor increments exponentially after the number of messages in the`DownwardMessageQueue`passes a threshold. This threshold is set as:
- [helpers](https://docs.rs/helpers/index.html)

- Implementation of a simple message queue. Used for sending messages. Simple mock message queue.

## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [__](https://docs.rs/macro.__impl_ext.html)- impl_ - ext
- Implements the `TestExt`trait for a specified struct.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_test_network.html)- test_ - network
- Declares a test network that consists of a relay chain and multiple
parachains. Expects a network struct as an argument and implements testing
functionality, `ParachainXcmRouter`and the`RelayChainXcmRouter`. The struct needs to contain the relay chain struct and an indexed list of parachains that are going to be in the network.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_test_parachain.html)- test_ - parachain
- The macro is implementing the `XcmMessageHandlerT`and`DmpMessageHandlerT`traits for the provided parachain struct. Expects the provided parachain struct to define the XcmpMessageHandler and DmpMessageHandler pallets that contain the message handling logic.
- [decl_](https://docs.rs/macro.decl_test_relay_chain.html)- test_ - relay_ - chain
- The macro is implementing upward message passing(UMP) for the provided relay chain struct. The struct has to provide the XCM configuration for the relay chain.

Check whether the given

`_message` is deliverable to the given `_destination` and if so
determine the cost which will be paid by this chain to do so, returning a `Validated` token
which can be used to enact delivery. [Read more](https://docs.rs/staging-xcm/24.0.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/staging_xcm/v5/traits/trait.SendXcm.html#tymethod.validate)## Auto Trait Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#synthetic-implementations)

# fission-accesskit-winit 0.33.1-fission.1 - Docs.rs

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/fission-accesskit-winit/0.33.1-fission.1

# AccessKit winit adapter

This is the winit adapter for [AccessKit](https://accesskit.dev/). It exposes an AccessKit accessibility tree through the platform-native accessibility API on any platform supported by AccessKit. On platforms not supported by AccessKit, this adapter does nothing, but still compiles.

## Compatibility with async runtimes

The following only applies on Linux/Unix:

While this crate's API is purely blocking, it internally spawns asynchronous tasks on an executor.

- If you use tokio, make sure to enable the `tokio`feature of this crate.
- If you use another async runtime or if you don't use one at all, the default feature will suit your needs.

## Android activity compatibility

The Android implementation of this adapter currently only works with [GameActivity](https://developer.android.com/games/agdk/game-activity), which is one of the two activity implementations that winit currently supports.

## Examples

The `examples/` directory contains two runnable examples:

- `simple`— a minimal window exposing a single accessible label.
- `mixed_handlers`— demonstrates combining AccessKit's action handling with winit event handling.

On desktop platforms, run them with `cargo run --example simple` or `cargo run --example mixed_handlers` from this crate's directory.

### Running the examples on iOS

Install [XcodeGen](https://github.com/yonaskolb/XcodeGen) and the iOS Rust targets, then run `xcodegen` from `examples/apple/` to generate the Xcode project. Open it in Xcode and build/run the `Simple` or `MixedHandlers` target on a device or simulator.

---

# accesskit - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/accesskit/^0.24.1/

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Action](https://docs.rs/struct.ActionRequest.html)- Request
- [Affine](https://docs.rs/struct.Affine.html)
- A 2D affine transform. Derived from [kurbo](https://github.com/linebender/kurbo).
- [Color](https://docs.rs/struct.Color.html)
- A color represented in 8-bit sRGB plus alpha.
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomAction.html)- Action
- Defines a custom action for a UI element.
- [Node](https://docs.rs/struct.Node.html)
- A single accessible object. A complete UI is represented as a tree of these.
- [NodeId](https://docs.rs/struct.NodeId.html)
- The stable identity of a `Node`
- [Point](https://docs.rs/struct.Point.html)
- A 2D point. Derived from [kurbo](https://github.com/linebender/kurbo).
- [Rect](https://docs.rs/struct.Rect.html)
- A rectangle. Derived from [kurbo](https://github.com/linebender/kurbo).
- [Size](https://docs.rs/struct.Size.html)
- A 2D size. Derived from [kurbo](https://github.com/linebender/kurbo).
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextDecoration.html)- Decoration
- The style and color for a type of text decoration.
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextPosition.html)- Position
- [Text](https://docs.rs/struct.TextSelection.html)- Selection
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/struct.Tree.html)
- The data associated with an accessibility tree that’s global to the tree and not associated with any particular node.
- [TreeId](https://docs.rs/struct.TreeId.html)
- The stable identity of a `Tree`
- [Tree](https://docs.rs/struct.TreeUpdate.html)- Update
- A serializable representation of an atomic change to a `Tree`
- [Uuid](https://docs.rs/struct.Uuid.html)
- A Universally Unique Identifier (UUID).
- [Vec2](https://docs.rs/struct.Vec2.html)
- A 2D vector. Derived from [kurbo](https://github.com/linebender/kurbo).

- The type of an accessibility node.

- A suggestion about where the node being scrolled into view should be positioned relative to the edges of the scrollable container.
- [Scroll](https://docs.rs/enum.ScrollUnit.html)- Unit

`Scroll`actions.
- [Sort](https://docs.rs/enum.SortDirection.html)- Direction

# raw_window_handle - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/^0.5/

## Expand description

Interoperability library for Rust Windowing applications.

This library provides standard types for accessing a window’s platform-specific raw window handle and platforms display handle. This does not provide any utilities for creating and managing windows; instead, it provides a common interface that window creation libraries (e.g. Winit, SDL) can use to easily talk with graphics libraries (e.g. gfx-hal).

Please see the docs of [ HasRawWindowHandle](https://docs.rs/trait.HasRawWindowHandle.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.HasRawDisplayHandle.html)

`HasRawDisplayHandle`Each platform handle struct is purposefully non-exhaustive, so that additional fields may be
added without breaking backwards compatibility. Each struct provides an `empty` method that may
be used along with the struct update syntax to construct it. See each specific struct for
examples.

Some windowing systems use a separate display handle for some operations. The display usually
represents a connection to some display server, but it is not necessarily tied to a particular
window. See [ RawDisplayHandle](https://docs.rs/enum.RawDisplayHandle.html) for more details.

- Keeps track of whether the application is currently active.
- Represents a live window handle.
- Raw display handle for Android.
- Raw window handle for Android NDK.
- Raw display handle for AppKit.
- Raw window handle for AppKit.
- The handle to the display controller of the windowing system.
- Raw display handle for the Linux Kernel Mode Set/Direct Rendering Manager.
- Raw window handle for the Linux Kernel Mode Set/Direct Rendering Manager.
- Raw display handle for the Linux Generic Buffer Manager.
- Raw window handle for the Linux Generic Buffer Manager.
- Raw display handle for Haiku.
- Raw window handle for Haiku.
- Raw display handle for the Redox operating system.
- Raw window handle for the Redox operating system.
- Raw display handle for UIKit.
- Raw window handle for UIKit.
- Raw display handle for Wayland.
- Raw window handle for Wayland.

- Raw window handle for the Web.

- Raw window handle for Xcb.

- Raw window handle for Xlib.

- The error type returned when a handle cannot be obtained.
- A display server handle for a particular windowing system.
- A window handle for a particular windowing system.

# raw_window_handle - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/^0.6.2/

## Expand description

Interoperability library for Rust Windowing applications.

This library provides standard types for accessing a window’s platform-specific raw window handle and platforms display handle. This does not provide any utilities for creating and managing windows; instead, it provides a common interface that window creation libraries (e.g. Winit, SDL) can use to easily talk with graphics libraries (e.g. gfx-hal).

[§](https://docs.rs#safety-guarantees)Safety guarantees

Please see the docs of [ HasWindowHandle](https://docs.rs/trait.HasWindowHandle.html) and

[.](https://docs.rs/trait.HasDisplayHandle.html)

`HasDisplayHandle`[§](https://docs.rs#platform-handle-initialization)Platform handle initialization

Each platform handle struct is purposefully non-exhaustive, so that additional fields may be
added without breaking backwards compatibility. Each struct provides an `empty` method that may
be used along with the struct update syntax to construct it. See each specific struct for
examples.

[§](https://docs.rs#display-handles)Display Handles

Some windowing systems use a separate display handle for some operations. The display usually
represents a connection to some display server, but it is not necessarily tied to a particular
window. See [ RawDisplayHandle](https://docs.rs/enum.RawDisplayHandle.html) for more details.

# winit - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/fission-winit/^0.30.13-fission.1/

## Expand description

Winit is a cross-platform window creation and event loop management library.

[§](https://docs.rs#building-windows)Building windows

Before you can create a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html), you first need to build an

[. This is done with the](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html)

`EventLoop`[function.](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html#method.new)

`EventLoop::new()````
use winit::event_loop::EventLoop;
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    // ...
}
```
Then you create a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html) with

[.](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.ActiveEventLoop.html#method.create_window)

`create_window`[§](https://docs.rs#event-handling)Event handling

Once a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html) has been created, it will generate different

*events*. A

[object can generate](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[s when certain input events occur, such as a cursor moving over the window or a key getting pressed while the window is focused. Devices can generate](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html)

`WindowEvent`[s, which contain unfiltered event data that isn’t specific to a certain window. Some user activity, like mouse movement, can generate both a](https://docs.rs/event/enum.DeviceEvent.html)

`DeviceEvent`

`WindowEvent`*and*a

[. You can also create and handle your own custom](https://docs.rs/event/enum.DeviceEvent.html)

`DeviceEvent`[s, if desired.](https://docs.rs/event/enum.Event.html#variant.UserEvent)

`Event::UserEvent`You can retrieve events by calling [ EventLoop::run_app()](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html#method.run_app). This function will
dispatch events for every

[that was created with that particular](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[, and will run until](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.EventLoop.html)

`EventLoop`[is used, at which point](https://docs.rs/event_loop/struct.ActiveEventLoop.html#method.exit)

`exit()`[.](https://docs.rs/event/enum.Event.html#variant.LoopExiting)

`Event::LoopExiting`Winit no longer uses a `EventLoop::poll_events() -> impl Iterator<Event>`-based event loop
model, since that can’t be implemented properly on some platforms (e.g web, iOS) and works
poorly on most other platforms. However, this model can be re-implemented to an extent with
`EventLoopExtPumpEvents::pump_app_events()` 1. See that method’s documentation for more reasons about why
it’s discouraged beyond compatibility reasons.

```
use winit::application::ApplicationHandler;
use winit::event::WindowEvent;
use winit::event_loop::{ActiveEventLoop, ControlFlow, EventLoop};
use winit::window::{Window, WindowId};
#[derive(Default)]
struct App {
    window: Option<Window>,
}
impl ApplicationHandler for App {
    fn resumed(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop) {
        self.window = Some(event_loop.create_window(Window::default_attributes()).unwrap());
    }
    fn window_event(&mut self, event_loop: &ActiveEventLoop, id: WindowId, event: WindowEvent) {
        match event {
            WindowEvent::CloseRequested => {
                println!("The close button was pressed; stopping");
                event_loop.exit();
            },
            WindowEvent::RedrawRequested => {
                // Redraw the application.
                //
                // It's preferable for applications that do not render continuously to render in
                // this event rather than in AboutToWait, since rendering in here allows
                // the program to gracefully handle redraws requested by the OS.
                // Draw.
                // Queue a RedrawRequested event.
                //
                // You only need to call this if you've determined that you need to redraw in
                // applications which do not always need to. Applications that redraw continuously
                // can render here instead.
                self.window.as_ref().unwrap().request_redraw();
            }
            _ => (),
        }
    }
}
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    // ControlFlow::Poll continuously runs the event loop, even if the OS hasn't
    // dispatched any events. This is ideal for games and similar applications.
    event_loop.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Poll);
    // ControlFlow::Wait pauses the event loop if no events are available to process.
    // This is ideal for non-game applications that only update in response to user
    // input, and uses significantly less power/CPU time than ControlFlow::Poll.
    event_loop.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Wait);
    let mut app = App::default();
    event_loop.run_app(&mut app);
}
```
[ WindowEvent](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html) has a

[member. In multi-window environments, it should be compared to the value returned by](https://docs.rs/window/struct.WindowId.html)

`WindowId`[to determine which](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.id)

`Window::id()`[dispatched the event.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html)

`Window`[§](https://docs.rs#drawing-on-the-window)Drawing on the window

Winit doesn’t directly provide any methods for drawing on a [ Window](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html). However, it allows you
to retrieve the raw handle of the window and display (see the

[module and/or the](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html)

`platform`[and](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.raw_window_handle)

`raw_window_handle`[methods), which in turn allows you to create an OpenGL/Vulkan/DirectX/Metal/etc. context that can be used to render graphics.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.raw_display_handle)

`raw_display_handle`Note that many platforms will display garbage data in the window’s client area if the
application doesn’t render anything to the window by the time the desktop compositor is ready to
display the window to the user. If you notice this happening, you should create the window with
[ visible set to false](https://docs.rs/window/struct.WindowAttributes.html#method.with_visible) and explicitly make
the window visible only once you’re ready to render into it.

[§](https://docs.rs#ui-scaling)UI scaling

UI scaling is important, go read the docs for the [ dpi](https://docs.rs/dpi/index.html) crate for an
introduction.

All of Winit’s functions return physical types, but can take either logical or physical coordinates as input, allowing you to use the most convenient coordinate system for your particular application.

Winit will dispatch a [ ScaleFactorChanged](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html#variant.ScaleFactorChanged) event whenever a window’s scale factor has changed.
This can happen if the user drags their window from a standard-resolution monitor to a high-DPI
monitor or if the user changes their DPI settings. This allows you to rescale your application’s
UI elements and adjust how the platform changes the window’s size to reflect the new scale
factor. If a window hasn’t received a

[event, its scale factor can be found by calling](https://docs.rs/event/enum.WindowEvent.html#variant.ScaleFactorChanged)

`ScaleFactorChanged`[.](https://docs.rs/window/struct.Window.html#method.scale_factor)

`window.scale_factor()`[§](https://docs.rs#cargo-features)Cargo Features

Winit provides the following Cargo features:

- `x11`(enabled by default): On Unix platforms, enables the X11 backend.
- `wayland`(enabled by default): On Unix platforms, enables the Wayland backend.
- `rwh_04`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.4`traits.
- `rwh_05`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.5`traits.
- `rwh_06`: Implement- `raw-window-handle v0.6`traits.
- `serde`: Enables serialization/deserialization of certain types with- [Serde](https://crates.io/crates/serde).
- `mint`: Enables mint (math interoperability standard types) conversions.

See the [ platform](https://docs.rs/platform/index.html) module for documentation on platform-specific cargo
features.

## Re-exports[§](https://docs.rs#reexports)

- `pub use`- [rwh_04](https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/0.6.2/i686-pc-windows-msvc/raw_window_handle/index.html)as raw_window_handle_04;- `rwh_04`
- `pub use`- [rwh_05](https://docs.rs/raw-window-handle/0.6.2/i686-pc-windows-msvc/raw_window_handle/index.html)as raw_window_handle_05;- `rwh_05`

# softbuffer - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/softbuffer/^0.4.8/

## Expand description

[§](https://docs.rs#softbuffer)Softbuffer

Enables software rendering via drawing an image straight to a window.

Softbuffer integrates with the [ raw-window-handle](https://crates.io/crates/raw-window-handle) crate
to allow writing pixels to a window in a cross-platform way while using the very high quality dedicated window management
libraries that are available in the Rust ecosystem.

[§](https://docs.rs#alternatives)Alternatives

[minifb](https://crates.io/crates/minifb) also allows putting a 2D buffer/image on a window in a platform-independent way.
Minifb’s approach to doing window management itself, however, is problematic code duplication. We already have very high quality
libraries for this in the Rust ecosystem (such as [winit](https://crates.io/crates/winit)), and minifb’s implementation
of window management is not ideal. For example, it occasionally segfaults and is missing key features such as setting
a window icon on some platforms. While adding these features to minifb would be possible, it makes more sense to use
the standard window handling systems instead.

What about [pixels](https://crates.io/crates/pixels)? Pixels accomplishes a very similar goal to Softbuffer,
however there are two key differences. Pixels provides some capacity for GPU-accelerated post-processing of what is
displayed, while Softbuffer does not. Due to not having this post-processing, Softbuffer does not rely on the GPU or
hardware accelerated graphics stack in any way, and is thus more portable to installations that do not have access to
hardware acceleration (e.g. VMs, older computers, computers with misconfigured drivers). Softbuffer should be used over
pixels when its GPU-accelerated post-processing effects are not needed.

[§](https://docs.rs#license--credits)License & Credits

This library is dual-licensed under MIT or Apache-2.0, just like minifb and rust. Significant portions of code were taken from the minifb library to do platform-specific work.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-support)Platform support:

Some, but not all, platforms supported in [raw-window-handle](https://crates.io/crates/raw-window-handle) are supported
by Softbuffer. Pull requests are welcome to add new platforms! **Nonetheless, all major desktop platforms that winit uses
on desktop are supported.**

For now, the priority for new platforms is:

- to have at least one platform on each OS working (e.g. one of Win32 or WinRT, or one of Xlib, Xcb, and Wayland) and
- for that one platform on each OS to be the one that winit uses.

(PRs will be accepted for any platform, even if it does not follow the above priority.)

| Platform | |
|---|---|
| Android NDK | ✅ |
| AppKit | ✅ |
| Orbital | ✅ |
| UIKit | ✅ |
| Wayland | ✅ |
| Web | ✅ |
| Win32 | ✅ |
| WinRT | ❌ |
| XCB | ✅ |
| Xlib | ✅ |

✅: Present

❔: Immature

❌: Absent

[§](https://docs.rs#webassembly)WebAssembly

To run an example with the web backend: `cargo run-wasm --example winit`

[§](https://docs.rs#android)Android

To run the Android-specific example on an Android phone: `cargo apk r --example winit_android` or `cargo apk r --example winit_multithread_android`.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
use std::num::NonZeroU32;
use std::rc::Rc;
use winit::event::{Event, WindowEvent};
use winit::event_loop::{ControlFlow, EventLoop};
use winit::window::Window;
#[path = "../examples/utils/winit_app.rs"]
mod winit_app;
fn main() {
    let event_loop = EventLoop::new().unwrap();
    let context = softbuffer::Context::new(event_loop.owned_display_handle()).unwrap();
    let mut app = winit_app::WinitAppBuilder::with_init(
        |elwt| {
            let window = elwt.create_window(Window::default_attributes());
            Rc::new(window.unwrap())
        },
        |_elwt, window| softbuffer::Surface::new(&context, window.clone()).unwrap(),
    )
    .with_event_handler(|window, surface, window_id, event, elwt| {
        elwt.set_control_flow(ControlFlow::Wait);
        if window_id != window.id() {
            return;
        }
        match event {
            WindowEvent::RedrawRequested => {
                let Some(surface) = surface else {
                    eprintln!("RedrawRequested fired before Resumed or after Suspended");
                    return;
                };
                let size = window.inner_size();
                surface
                    .resize(
                        NonZeroU32::new(size.width).unwrap(),
                        NonZeroU32::new(size.height).unwrap(),
                    )
                    .unwrap();
                let mut buffer = surface.buffer_mut().unwrap();
                for index in 0..(buffer.width().get() * buffer.height().get()) {
                    let y = index / buffer.width().get();
                    let x = index % buffer.width().get();
                    let red = x % 255;
                    let green = y % 255;
                    let blue = (x * y) % 255;
                    buffer[index as usize] = blue | (green << 8) | (red << 16);
                }
                buffer.present().unwrap();
            }
            WindowEvent::CloseRequested => {
                elwt.exit();
            }
            _ => {}
        }
    });
    event_loop.run_app(&mut app).unwrap();
}
```
[§](https://docs.rs#msrv-policy)MSRV Policy

This crate’s Minimum Supported Rust Version (MSRV) is **1.71**. Changes to
the MSRV will be accompanied by a minor version bump.

As a **tentative** policy, the upper bound of the MSRV is given by the following
formula:

`min(sid, stable - 3)`Where `sid` is the current version of `rustc` provided by [Debian Sid](https://packages.debian.org/sid/rustc), and
`stable` is the latest stable version of Rust. This bound may be broken in case of a major ecosystem shift or a security vulnerability.

Orbital is not covered by this MSRV policy, as it requires a Rust nightly toolchain to compile.

All crates in the [ rust-windowing](https://github.com/rust-windowing) organizations have the
same MSRV policy.

See the [changelog](https://docs.rs/CHANGELOG.md) for a list of this package’s versions and the changes made in each version.

# accesskit_ios - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/accesskit_ios/^0.1.1/

## Expand description

iOS adapter for AccessKit.

This crate provides two adapters for exposing an AccessKit accessibility tree to iOS via UIKit’s accessibility API:

-
`Adapter``isAccessibilityElement`,`accessibilityElements`,`accessibilityHitTest:`) from your`UIView`subclass to the adapter. Use this when you own the`UIView`subclass and can override these methods directly.
-
`SubclassingAdapter``Adapter``UIView`. Use this when you cannot subclass the view yourself, for example when integrating with a framework that creates views on your behalf.

## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [Adapter](https://docs.rs/struct.Adapter.html)
- An AccessKit adapter for an owned `UIView`.
- [CGPoint](https://docs.rs/struct.CGPoint.html)
- A point in a two-dimensional coordinate system.
- [NSArray](https://docs.rs/struct.NSArray.html)
- [NSObject](https://docs.rs/struct.NSObject.html)
- The root class of most Objective-C class hierarchies.
- [Queued](https://docs.rs/struct.QueuedEvents.html)- Events
- Events generated by a tree update.
- [Subclassing](https://docs.rs/struct.SubclassingAdapter.html)- Adapter
- Uses dynamic Objective-C subclassing to implement the `UIView`accessibility methods when normal subclassing isn’t an option.
